newsitem.title: FALKLAND ISLANDS: Falklanders angry over Argentine birthday call.
newsitem.headline: Falklanders angry over Argentine birthday call.

text.p: Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella has angered Falkland Islanders by promoting his political "charm offensive" on the birthday of Britain's Queen Elizabeth.

Di Tella, who has sent Christmas gifts and messages to the inhabitants of the disputed archipelago, sent them a letter on the queen's 71st birthday, saying "I am doing so as an expression of respect to you, your loyalties and your feelings."
What angered the islanders was the final paragraph of his letter.

"I would like to repeat my sincere belief that we are getting closer to the point where differences ought to be addressed. I am sure that if we do that, we will find a mutually acceptable solution. I think we all now understand better our respective positions, limitations and possibilities," he wrote.
That sparked protests from islanders who gathered in Port Stanley on Monday for a parade to mark the queen's birthday.

"I am disgusted that Di Tella could use our Queen's birthday to once again force his political rhetoric upon us. Today is a day of celebration for us and not an occasion to be reminded of Argentina's spurious claim," said Bill Williams, 52.
Councillor William Luxton said Di Tella was "living in cloud cuckoo land. The man is so totally out of touch with reality that it just isn't true.
"Sending a stupid political message to us on the occasion of our Queen's birthday will if anything help the Falklands, as people will see his action as being inappropriate and crass," he added.
Argentina and Britain fought a 10-week war over the islands in 1982. Although Argentina lost, it maintains its claim to the sparsely inhabited archipelago, which it calls the Malvinas.
The two countries have since restored diplomatic relations and in 1995 signed a deal to explore for oil in waters surrounding the Falklands.
